learning_objective: 🎯 Bridge the gap between the classroom and the real world! Learn how to translate real-life problems into math equations, solve them, and interpret the results.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is the process of taking a messy, real-world problem (like predicting traffic or calculating interest on a bank loan) and writing it entirely as a mathematical equation or formula.

The real world is too complex to calculate perfectly. We have to make 'Assumptions' to simplify it. For example, if modelling a car trip, we assume the car drives at a constant speed, even though in reality it stops at red lights.

The 4 steps: 
1. Formulate: Turn the real problem into a math problem. 
2. Solve: Do the math to find an answer. 
3. Interpret: Turn the math answer back into a real-world meaning. 
4. Validate: Check if the answer actually makes sense in real life.

fun_activity.title: 📝 Model Your Morning
fun_activity.instructions: Model the time it takes to get to school. Variables: $w$ (wake up time), $b$ (breakfast time in mins), $t$ (travel time). Math formula: Total Time = $b + t$. Assumption: We assume there is no unexpected traffic today. If your math answer says you'll arrive at 8:00 AM, 'Validate' it tomorrow by checking your watch when you arrive!

exam_tips: 📌 Always clearly state your 'Assumptions' before writing the mathematical equation. Examiners look for this to see if you understand the limits of your model.
📌 In the 'Validation' step, if your math predicts that a car journey takes negative 5 hours, your model has failed. Validation is the reality check!
📌 Be ready to translate a word problem into a linear equation as part of the 'Formulate' step.
quick_recap: ⭐ Mathematical modelling uses equations to represent and solve real-world scenarios.
⭐ Assumptions are necessary to simplify complex real-life variables into solvable math.
⭐ A successful model must be formulated, solved, interpreted, and rigorously validated against reality.
